content:
Hello everyone,

I'm Dmitrii Semenov, an independent researcher (no institution), posting here for the first time. I've been building a Lean 4 formalization and would love feedback from this community.

It's organised around a single prohibition: the impossibility of an infinite "clean" descent (a "perpetual engine") — a version of Fermat's infinite descent, restated for the centres of the pairs 6m±1. From that one fact it derives a machine-checked reduction of the twin-prime conjecture to a single explicit open node, and reads several well-known conjectures (RH, P vs NP, Yang–Mills, Hodge, Navier–Stokes, BSD, plus Mersenne/Collatz) through the same lens.

To be completely clear about scope: nothing is solved. The whole development rests on exactly one clearly-quarantined axiom and contains exactly one sorry (the twin-prime conjecture itself). A script (scripts/VerifyAll.lean) re-checks these two invariants on every build and reports the axiom-taint count. The RH / Millennium material is honest reductions and one decree, never a proof.

  • Source (Lean 4): https://github.com/elamaunt/Euclids-path
  • Archived release (Zenodo): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21198731
  • Write-up (every theorem names its Lean declaration): https://elamaunt.github.io/Euclids-path/en/

I'd genuinely welcome scrutiny of the quarantine/verifier setup and any pointers on mathlib idioms I've missed. Thank you!

Best,
Dmitrii
